kjv: Save when there shall be no poor among you
mine: There will, however, be no poor among you
note: Hebrew 'ephes ki here introduces a strong assertion ("but indeed / nevertheless") that there will be no poor if Israel obeys; the KJV's "save when" turns it into a restriction on the release law, which then sits awkwardly with v. 11.

kjv: a thought in thy wicked heart
mine: no base thought in your heart
note: The adjective beliyya'al ("worthless, base") goes with davar ("thing, thought"), not with "heart": the warning is against a mean-spirited calculation, not a description of the heart itself.
Hebrew 'eved 'olam here means a permanent slave for the rest of his life; "for ever" is literal for 'olam but the sense is lifelong.
